title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page (Grothendieck's p.402, start of §IV, 'Les trois cas particuliers fondamentaux') belongs to the sequel of La Longue Marche, written c.1981, on the 'équation des lacets'. The objects are as follows.
- π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1−{0,1,∞}. π̃_{0,3}^ is its extension by the symmetry group S_3 of the three punctures (generated by an involution σ_∞ fixing ∞ and a 3-cycle ρ). Equivalently it is the profinite orbifold fundamental group of the quotient of P^1−{0,1,∞} by S_3.
- u is an element of the group M^{!~}_{0,3} of (suitably normalized) automorphisms of π̃_{0,3}^ compatible with the S_3-structure. The Galois group maps into this group.
- u can be encoded by four equivalent data (92): (g,h,f), (α_0,β_0,f), (α,β,f), (ξ,η,f). Here f is the basic 'Drinfeld-type' element of π̂_{0,3}. The others are the defects measuring how u fails to commute with the generators σ_∞ and ρ.

First special case (93)–(94). The following are equivalent: h=1, β_0=1, β=f, η=fσ_∞(f)^{-1}, and [u,σ_∞]=1. So the first special case is exactly the subgroup of automorphisms commuting with the involution σ_∞.

Normalization lemma. For an arbitrary u there is one and only one inner automorphism int(γ) such that u'=int(γ)u commutes with σ_∞, namely γ=β_0^{-1} (cf. formulas (49)). Uniqueness is correct: the centralizer of σ_∞ in π̂_{0,3} is trivial. Geometrically, the quotient of P^1−{0,1,∞} by z↦1−z is an orbifold with orbifold group Z/2 * Z. In a free (profinite) product, a finite free factor is self-centralizing (Herfort–Ribes in the profinite case). So the normalization is unique. This is the normalization at the rational point 1/2, the fixed point of σ_∞; on the next page the subgroup is named M^{!~}_{0,3}(1/2).

Parametrization. In this normalized case u is given by triples (ξ,η,f) satisfying relations (44)–(46). Since η=fσ_∞(f)^{-1} is forced, u is equivalently given by pairs (ξ,f) in π̂_{0,3} with:
- (95) ξ·ρ(f)·ρ²(f)=1, a 3-cycle ('hexagon'-type) relation;
- (96) ξ=(fσ_∞(f)^{-1})·l_1^ν, with ν∈Ẑ and 2ν+1∈Ẑ*. The cyclotomic parameter is thus λ=2ν+1, exactly Drinfeld's later λ=2m+1.

A marginal NB gives ξ = f g ρ(f)^{-1} (reading uncertain). The next page rewrites everything as pairs (α,β) satisfying the loop equation αρ(α)^{-1}=βσ_∞(β)^{-1}b^ν. It shows such u normalize the subalgebra of M_2(Ẑ) generated by σ_∞ on abelianized homology, using τ_∞(σ_∞)=−σ_∞.

The 'three fundamental cases' are presumably the normalizations at the three special orbifold points of (P^1−{0,1,∞})/S_3 = the j-line:
- the order-2 point λ=1/2 (j=1728);
- the order-3 point e^{iπ/3} (j=0);
- the cusp (tangential base point).

Purpose: to reduce the description of the Galois/GT-type automorphism group to normalized forms in which the loop equation becomes Drinfeld-style 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations.
errors: No mathematical error detectable on this page. The uniqueness claim for int(γ) is correct because the involution σ_∞ is self-centralizing in the profinite orbifold group Z/2 ⨿ Ẑ. Whether one needs uniqueness of γ or only of int(γ) is moot, since π̂_{0,3} is centerless.

Relation (95) as transcribed (ξρ(f)ρ²(f)=1) cannot be independently checked against (44)–(46), which are not on this page. The exact form of (96) (the generator l_1 and the placement of the power ν) is partly illegible.

ideas.what: Normalizing an automorphism of the profinite π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) ⋊ S_3 by a unique inner automorphism so that it commutes with the involution σ_∞ (z↦1−z); this is equivalent to a 2-cycle relation on f.
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of GT elements; the 2-cycle relation f(x,y)f(y,x)=1; base point at 1/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for the GT relations; Ihara (1990s) for the profinite GT; Nakamura and others for Galois actions with base point 1/2 / orbifold points
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981, circulated); this explicit normalization is not there as far as I know

ideas.what: Parametrizing the normalized automorphisms by pairs (ξ,f) with a 3-cycle relation ξρ(f)ρ²(f)=1 and ξ=fσ_∞(f)^{-1}l^ν, with cyclotomic parameter λ=2ν+1∈Ẑ*.
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon / 3-cycle relation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group with λ=2m+1
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche contains early forms of the loop equation; this exact form is unsure

ideas.what: Viewing the 'three fundamental particular cases' as the normalizations at the three special points of the S_3-quotient (order-2 point, order-3 point, cusp).
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT actions relative to orbifold base points of the j-line (j=1728, j=0, ∞)

missed.claim: Around 1981, a decade before Drinfeld, Grothendieck normalizes the automorphisms in his loop-equation group so that they commute with the involution of P^1−{0,1,∞}. He obtains relations equivalent in shape to the 2-cycle and 3-cycle relations of GT, with the cyclotomic parameter written λ=2ν+1.
missed.quote: il y a un et un seul int(γ) tel que u' = int(γ)u satisfasse la propriété précédente i.e. commute à σ_∞, ce sera pour γ = β_0^{-1} ... avec ν ∈ Ẑ ... tel que 2ν+1 ∈ Ẑ*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is documentary evidence that the defining GT relations, including Drinfeld's exact parametrization λ=2m+1, were essentially present in Grothendieck's unpublished 1981 notes. It is relevant to the history and attribution of GT.

missed.claim: A systematic treatment of 'three fundamental cases': normalizing at the order-2 point (1/2), the order-3 point and the cusp, each giving a subgroup M_{0,3}(1/2) etc. isomorphic to the full group, and comparing the resulting parametrizations.
missed.quote: IV Les trois cas particuliers fondamentaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparison maps between GT parametrizations at different orbifold base points of the j-line are only partially treated in the literature. Grothendieck's explicit change-of-normalization formulas could be useful.

deep.surprise_reason: The page cleanly anticipates Drinfeld's GT normalization: the 2-cycle condition is interpreted as commuting with σ_∞ at base point 1/2, and λ=2ν+1 appears explicitly. That the Longue Marche contains GT-like ideas is known to specialists (e.g. Schneps), but this explicit three-base-point normalization in the less-studied sequel is a notable unpublished detail.
